name: caller-derivation
description: Run the ledger's own ContractCall::context derivation over the real composed bytes of the write_then_read call transaction, captured at every stage and submitted, and record what caller resolves to per call frame
note: Observed: the ledger's own ContractCall::context, at tag ledger-9.1.0.0-rc.3, run off-node over real composed bytes, resolves Tally set and get to Contract(<Caller address>) and the root write_then_read to None. NOT observed: a node evaluating a slot-6 read, because Compact has no reader for context slot 6 and no circuit in this experiment reads it, so these are the values the ledger computes and marshals into that slot rather than values a contract was seen to receive. That holds on all 4 captures [offline-unproven 2872 B, unproven 2878 B, proven 10285 B, balanced 13560 B]: 8 sub-call frames resolve to Contract(<the address of the root call in the same intent>) and 4 root frames to None, across 4 call-carrying intents whose unshielded offers are all absent, so the User arm could not fire; the Caller addresses observed were 7c746d8429c1a5266774bdc3d88ab5e48c4f0d97b6aabd290192b980d33e5502 and d2938fa034b5843667cd7609f85042cd417585f229d1ac31113da68b532f675f (the offline arm derives its own pair). The Rust and TypeScript views of the same bytes agree on every address, entry point, communication commitment, and claim; offline construction POSSIBLE (no node, no indexer); submitted as 0016a72ceb30914e… (SucceedEntirely).

offline.addressesFrom: offline deploy (ContractDeploy.address of locally built deploy transactions; NOT the live pair)

rustCallerDerivation.expectation: the Tally set and get calls resolve to Contract(<Caller address>); the root write_then_read call, in an intent with no unshielded inputs, resolves to None
